## About
RHS Roofing is a roofing contractor on E McKellips Rd in Mesa, Arizona. Michelle R. is the owner, and Anthony R. handles sales and estimates. We take on minor repairs, full roof replacements and anything in between, for homes and for commercial buildings.
Our customers tend to mention the same things: Anthony explains the plan before work starts, the crew shows up on time, and the price is fair. One commercial property manager calls us their go-to and says they've worked with the owners, Tony and Michelle, for years.
We're rated 4.4 on Google from 20 reviews. If you're not sure whether you need a repair or a new roof, call us and we'll come take a look.

## Services
- Roof repair: From quick fixes to minor repairs, handled with the same care as a full job.
- Roof replacement: Full tear-off and replacement, with updates from Anthony along the way.
- Tile roofing: Durable, long-lasting roofs using individual tiles of clay, concrete or slate.
- Shingle roofing: A common, dependable choice for residential homes.
- Foam roofing: A lightweight, seamless system made from spray-applied polyurethane foam (SPF).
- Rolled roofing: A budget-friendly material that comes in large rolls, typically asphalt or mineral-surfaced.
- O’Hagin Vents: For better ventilation in your attic. You can also save by buying a package. ($349 each)
- Solar removal and reinstall: One reviewer had his solar panels taken off and put back on as part of his roof job.

## FAQ
Q: How do I know if I need a roof replacement or just a repair?
A: If your roof is leaking, has missing or damaged shingles, or shows signs of wear, an inspection is the best way to tell. Age, extent of damage and overall condition all factor in.

Q: How long does a roof replacement take?
A: It depends on the size of the roof, the materials and the weather. On average, a residential roof replacement takes anywhere from 1 to 3 days.

Q: How much does a new roof cost?
A: It varies with materials, roof size and how complex the install is. Asphalt shingles are typically the more affordable option, while tile, metal and foam can cost more. Contact us for a free, detailed estimate.

Q: Are you licensed, bonded, and insured?
A: Yes. We are fully licensed, bonded, and insured, so you're protected throughout the job and the work meets state and local regulations.

Q: How often should I have my roof inspected?
A: At least once a year and after major storms. Regular inspections catch problems early and help your roof last longer.
